newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Jail term for S.African rightist who beat blacks.
newsitem.headline: Jail term for S.African rightist who beat blacks.

text.p: South African white supremacist Eugene Terre Blanche was sentenced to six years in jail on Tuesday for trying to murder one black man and assaulting another.

"On count one, the accused is sentenced to six years imprisonment. On charge two, the accused is sentenced to a period of one year imprisonment, which will be served concurrently," said magistrate Chris Eksteen.

Terre Blanche, leader of the neo-Nazi Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB), was impassive and his supporters in the court in Potchefstroom, southwest of Johannesburg, were subdued as he stood to hear the magistrate pronounce sentence.
Eksteen rebuked the khaki-clad right-winger for a show of anger when judgment was handed down in April.

"The outburst in this court during the judgment confirms the impressions that the court gained from the state witnesses that the accused is a person who easily resorts to violence and tolerates no opposition," he said.
Terre Blanche, 53, had shown no genuine remorse, he added.
The magistrate also ruled that Terre Blanche be prohibited from owning any firearms.
The rightist leader asked to be allowed to appeal against the sentence and conviction, and his lawyers asked for him to be granted bail of 5,000 rand ($1,100).
The magistrate said this amount was too low, and ordered court to reconvene at 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) to consider a higher amount.
Several dozen rightists gathered at the court to show their support, but a larger group of blacks sang and some waved placards demanding a life jail term for Terre Blanche.
Scores of police guarded the courtroom, which was sealed off by razor-wire.

The supremacist leader rallied thousands of rightists behind his cause during negotiations to end apartheid in the early 1990s, but his support has waned in recent years largely because of South Africa's peaceful transition to majority rule, instead of the bloodbath he had forecast.
